c.tagline: A belle-époque spa town on the edge of the Black Forest, where thermal baths and a grand casino have drawn European royalty for two centuries

card: Contactless and card payment are the norm at hotels, restaurants, and the casino; small cafes, market stalls, and some spa facilities may prefer cash, so carry a little euros.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; airport transfers to Karlsruhe/Baden-Baden Airport or Stuttgart are usually flat-rate — confirm before boarding

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and reaches English-speaking dispatchers in most cases

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: The compact spa-town core between the Kurhaus, casino, and Lichtentaler Allee is entirely walkable and pedestrian-friendly; the Old Town's hillside lanes involve some gentle climbing, and Merkur mountain is reached by a short funicular rather than on foot.

safety.safety: Very safe; Baden-Baden is a genteel resort town with very low crime and is comfortable for solo travelers at any hour
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main caution is standard care with valuables in busy tourist areas like the casino and spa lockers

hood_landmark.Altstadt (Old Town): Stiftskirche and the New Castle hillside
hood_landmark.Lichtental: Lichtentaler Allee promenade and Kloster Lichtenthal abbey
hood_landmark.Weststadt / Rebland: Vineyard slopes toward the Rhine valley

hood_desc: The elegant heart of the spa town, centered on the Kurhaus, casino, and grand 19th-century hotels — the natural base for most visitors and home to the thermal baths.
The hillside medieval core above the spa quarter, with narrow lanes, the Stiftskirche, and the New Castle offering panoramic views over the town.
A quiet, leafy district along the Lichtentaler Allee promenade, anchored by the historic Cistercian abbey and rose gardens — a peaceful, residential contrast to the casino district.
The wine-growing fringe toward the Rhine valley, dotted with vineyards and a more local, less touristy pace.
A hilltop village a short drive or hike above town, known for its ruined castle and sweeping Black Forest views.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Contactless card, KVV app, or cash on board; day tickets available
transit.map: Route maps at kvv.de and posted at bus stops
transit.note: The compact center is easily walkable; buses mainly serve outlying districts like Ebersteinburg and Rebland

transport.air: Baden-Baden Karlsruhe Airport (FKB), ~10 km away, with flights on Ryanair and others to European cities; Stuttgart Airport (STR) is a larger alternative about 1 hour away
transport.train: Baden-Baden station has ICE high-speed connections to Frankfurt (~1.5 hrs), Basel, and Karlsruhe; the station is about 15 minutes from the town center by bus or taxi
transport.bus: FlixBus and regional coaches connect Baden-Baden to Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, and Strasbourg
transport.ferry: None — Baden-Baden is inland with no ferry service
transport.car: Easily reached via the A5 autobahn; parking in the compact center is limited, so many hotels offer valet or garage parking

airport.name: Baden-Baden Karlsruhe Airport
airport.transport: Airport shuttle bus timed to flights; taxi transfer roughly €25-35

net.m: Excellent 4G/5G coverage throughout Baden-Baden and the surrounding Black Forest foothills
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels, cafes, and the Kurhaus
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes and public spaces in the town center
net.ap: EU roaming covers most European visitors; a prepaid German SIM or eSIM is easy to buy at the airport or a phone shop for others

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up or a small tip for spa attendants and hotel staff is appreciated
tip.r: 5-10% is customary if service isn't already included — hand the tip directly to the server rather than leaving it on the table
